question: How does each of the five define and report advisor headcount -- and what does each definition include or exclude?

claims.text: Edward Jones - The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) reports "Financial advisors (actual)" at year end of 20,425 (2025), 20,125 (2024) and 19,232 (2023), and an average of 20,331 (2025), 19,650 (2024) and 18,945 (2023). So it reports both a period-end and an average count.

Edward Jones - In the Q3 2025 10-Q (published 2025-11-07), the firm describes its "more than 20,000 financial advisors" as of September 26, 2025, in a Partnership that operates in the U.S. and Canada.

Edward Jones - The Q3 2025 10-Q defines "Attrition %" as the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period, compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end. Departures and retirements are therefore counted, and the denominator is the period-end headcount.

Raymond James - The fiscal 2025 10-K (period ended 2025-09-30, published 2025-11-25) says the number of financial advisors increased year over year because new recruits and trainees moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements. Trainees are therefore counted once they move into production roles.
Raymond James - The same 10-K says advisors in the RCS division are not included in the financial advisor metric, although their client assets are included in PCG AUA. This is an explicit exclusion.
Raymond James - On the fiscal Q4 2025 call (transcript published 2025-10-22), the CEO cited a record number of financial advisors of 8,943.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's January 2026 strategic update and its 10-K define "Advisor-Led Client Assets" as client assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned. Advisor-Led Households are households with at least one account holding such assets.
adjacent.differs_because: These definitions count client assets and households tied to an assigned representative. They do not count or define advisors.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's Q3 2026 GWIM deck and press release define Merrill households as those with $250K+ in investible assets, excluding stock plan and banking-only households. The Private Bank covers relationships with $3MM+ in total balances.
adjacent.differs_because: These are client household and relationship definitions for the GWIM segment, which includes both Merrill and the Private Bank. They are not advisor headcount definitions.

adjacent.text: Schwab's Q1 2026 10-Q attributes higher compensation and benefits expense in Investor Services and Advisor Services partly to "growth in headcount".
adjacent.differs_because: This is general employee headcount mentioned as a cost driver. It is not a defined or reported advisor count.

adjacent.text: On the Q1 2025 call (April 2025), Schwab's CEO said the firm expected to open around 16 new branches that year.
adjacent.differs_because: This is a branch expansion plan. It does not define or report advisor headcount.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley: an advisor headcount figure and its definition (who is counted or excluded) are not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley 10-K or quarterly financial supplement, Wealth Management key metrics and footnotes (financial advisor or representative counts)

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America 10-K / GWIM segment disclosures and Merrill Lynch investor materials

gaps.what: Merrill: an advisor headcount figure and its definition are not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America 10-K or earnings supplement GWIM key indicators (financial advisor counts)

gaps.what: Schwab: a defined and reported advisor headcount, and its inclusions and exclusions, are not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab 10-K business section or investor day materials covering Advisor Services and wealth advisory (advisor or financial consultant counts)

gaps.what: Edward Jones: the 10-K figures do not state which individuals the "financial advisors (actual)" count includes or excludes, for example trainees or Canadian advisors. Only the attrition definition is given.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones 10-K Item 1 Business and MD&A footnotes on financial advisor definitions

gaps.what: Neither firm discloses advisor attrition on a comparable basis. Edward Jones defines an attrition % and Raymond James does not, in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James 10-K / investor presentations on advisor departures; Edward Jones 10-K
